title: Two pendulums and a pen can draw spirals all by themselves

cover.alt: A wooden harmonograph: a sheet of paper on a board hanging from chains, with a green pen on a wooden arm resting on a faint looping drawing.
cover.credit: Matemateca (IME/USP), Rodrigo Tetsuo Argenton · CC BY-SA 4.0

body: A **harmonograph** turns swinging into drawing. In the simplest kind, one pendulum moves a pen back and forth while a second moves the paper at right angles to it, so the line on the page adds the two swings together into a **Lissajous curve**. Change how fast each pendulum swings, or how far out of step they are, and you get an ellipse, a figure eight or something far more elaborate. Friction makes every swing a little smaller than the last, so the loops shrink as they go and curl into spirals.

slides.alt: A board of paper hanging from chains sways under a green pen held on a wooden arm. Then, close up, a second pen sits at the centre of a drawing of nested loops that close in towards it.
slides.caption: A harmonograph in Matemateca, the maths collection of the University of São Paulo. Paper on a board hung from chains swings under a pen, and as the swings die away the loops close in on the centre.
slides.credit: Matemateca (IME/USP), Rodrigo Tetsuo Argenton · CC BY-SA 4.0 · excerpt
slides.music: “Canon in D for Two Harps” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.prompt: With just two pendulums, one moving the pen and one the paper, what shapes can a harmonograph draw?
slides.detail: All of them are Lissajous figures, and adding more pendulums, or hanging one pendulum from another, gives even more complex drawings.

slides.heading: Why the loops spiral in
slides.text: Each pendulum swings like a sine wave, `A sin(ft + p)`, where f sets how fast it swings and p where it starts. Friction adds a fading factor, `e^(−dt)`, so every swing is a little smaller. The pattern keeps its shape but shrinks, and a closed loop becomes a spiral.

slides.question: What makes a harmonograph’s loops shrink into a spiral?
options: The pen slowly runs out of ink
The paper is pulled to the centre
slides.explanation: The pendulums are damped: friction takes a little energy from every swing, so each loop is smaller than the one before.
